title: feat(slack): use Slack-flavored markdown blocks for reply rendering
body:
## Summary

Switches reply body rendering from `section`/`mrkdwn` blocks to Slack's native [`markdown` block](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/blocks/markdown-block) (`{type: "markdown"}`). This block accepts Slack-flavored Markdown (**bold**, *italic*, [links](url), headings, code blocks, lists) and Slack renders it natively — fixing the inconsistent formatting where `**bold**` and `[text](url)` would show up as literal text in mrkdwn sections.

**Key changes:**
- `footer.ts`: `buildSlackReplyBlocks()` emits `{type: "markdown"}` for the body (instead of `{type: "section", text: {type: "mrkdwn"}}`)
- `reply.ts`: ALL reply chunks get markdown blocks (not just the last one with footer); `text` field passes raw markdown as notification preview
- `prompt.ts`: Updated output format to instruct Slack-flavored Markdown (`**bold**`, `[text](url)`, `# heading`) instead of legacy mrkdwn
- Spec: Updated `slack-outbound-contract-spec.md` with new rendering contract

**Architecture:**
- Displayed message → `{type: "markdown", text: "**bold** [link](url)"}` — Slack renders natively
- Notification preview → `text` field passes raw markdown (no conversion layer needed)
- Footer → stays as `{type: "context"}` blocks with mrkdwn (simple label: value pairs)

The `markdown` block is available to apps with the "Agents & AI Apps" feature enabled (which Junior already has — we use `assistant.threads.setStatus`).

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Deploy to staging and verify a reply with **bold**, `code`, and a `[link](url)` renders correctly in Slack (not as literal markdown)
- [ ] Confirm the markdown block doesn't error for the Junior Slack app (requires Agents & AI Apps feature — already enabled)
- [ ] Check push notifications show the raw text preview (acceptable tradeoff vs. adding a conversion layer)

### Notes

The 12,000 character cumulative limit per message payload for markdown blocks is well within our chunk budget (max ~2,200 chars per chunk).
